summary.tldr: Amends the Investment Canada Act to add new notice, review, information-sharing, and penalty rules for some investments with national security implications.
what_it_does: Requires notice of certain investments before they are carried out.
Lets the Minister of Industry, after consulting the Minister of Public Safety and Emergency Preparedness, impose interim conditions during a review to prevent possible harm to national security.
Lets the Minister of Industry order further review of investments under Part IV.1 and accept written undertakings to address national security risks.
Adds rules to protect information in judicial review cases about decisions and orders under Part IV.1.
Lets the Minister of Industry share otherwise privileged information with foreign states for foreign investment reviews.

Sets a new penalty of up to the greater of $500,000 and any prescribed amount for failing to give notice or file required applications, and raises daily penalties for other breaches to the greater of $25,000 and any prescribed amount.
who_it_affects: Minister of Public Safety and Emergency Preparedness
summary.background: The bill amends the Investment Canada Act. It was introduced in the House of Commons on 7 December 2022.
